sentences.text: Gasoline vapor is heavier than air, so it flows downhill and collects in the bilge and low compartments, where a single spark from a switch, pump or starter can ignite it.
A surprisingly small amount of vaporized gasoline can produce an explosion strong enough to destroy a boat.
Diesel fuel is much less volatile and much harder to ignite, which is one reason most commercial boats run diesel, but it still burns once lit.
Most boat explosions happen during or just after fueling.
